newsitem.title: USA: EDS CFO sees single digit Q1 revs growth.
newsitem.headline: EDS CFO sees single digit Q1 revs growth.

text.p: Electronic Data Systems Corp. expects its revenues to grow in the high single digits in the first quarter of 1997, Chief Financial Officer Jody Grant said.

"We believe it will be high single digits. We hope we might experience double digit base business revenue growth but, taking the conservative approach, we'd say there is a reasonable possibility that they could be single digits," Grant said in a telephone interview.

Grant said the relatively moderate revenue growth, which is below EDS' historic levels, was in part due to the slow pace of new business contracts won in early 1996 and expected to kick in in the coming months.
"Our new business signings in the first half of 1996 were relatively soft and it will take us a while to ramp up the very good last six months that we had in 1996," he said.

The Texas-based company earlier said its fourth quarter profits were $272.8 million, or $0.56 per share, compared to $269.5 million, or $0.56 per share, in the same period in 1995. Revenues rose to $4.01 billion from $3.62 billion.
EDS was spun off from General Motors Corp last June, 12 years after it was first sold to the auto giant.
Under the spinoff deal, EDS was freed to seek contracts with GM's competitors but more and more of the services it supplied to GM will be put out to competitive bid.
Grant said revenues earned from GM contracts, which account for 30 percent of total EDS revenues, had been stronger than expected in the second half of 1996 but would likely slow in 1997.
"We would expect that GM revenues would be probably relatively flat and possibly even be down some from 1996," he said.
